persistence_invariants.brief: The up migration (add batch_number/serial_number, backfill, drop inventory_code) has a down migration that re-adds inventory_code and reconstructs it from location + batch + serial; up then down leaves the schema and every row round-tripped.
The UNIQUE(sku, location) key established in F1 survives this migration unchanged; splitting the code neither drops nor duplicates the constraint and location stays the canonical addressing column.

batch_number and serial_number are added as NULLABLE (no NOT NULL): nonconforming codes must persist as NULL rather than being defaulted or forcing the row out, so the columns carry no NOT NULL constraint.
Every pre-migration stock row (quantity, sku, location) is still present and retrievable after the up migration; no row is dropped whether or not its code parsed.

nfrs.brief: Every sprint-1 stock row survives the schema refactor with no loss: conforming codes backfill batch/serial, nonconforming codes persist with NULL batch/serial, and no row is dropped. Defended by real-branch integrity tests on the migrated table.
UNIQUE(sku, location) is preserved through the migration; location remains canonical and is never overwritten from the code's leading segment.

All acceptance tests run against the paired Lakebase branch (databricks_postgres via DATABASE_URL) with Alembic migrations applied to the branch; no mock, stub, or in-memory DB. Both up and down migrations are exercised on the real branch.

The migration is reversible: the down path reconstructs inventory_code from location + batch + serial and restores the combined column, enabling rollback during rollout (additive-where-possible preference).

A migration-time integrity probe reports the count of nonconforming rows (codes that could not be parsed into batch and serial) for review before the change is accepted; delimiter-only parsing, no fabrication.
N/A for S1 (a headless schema migration with no UI surface); the boundary stays a React SPA + JSON API for the downstream S2 view story, inheriting the F1 convention. No server-rendered HTML.
